evidence: server/http/shutdown.ts:74-86 runs beginShutdown, socketAdapterReady, io.close, settleDisconnects, then closeOwnership (drops every lock) while activeGames still holds the games. server/game/gameTimers.ts arm() (line ~58) and gameTurn.ts runBotTurn/startAfkTimer never read isShuttingDown (it is read only at tableHandlers.ts:661,813,819, tableRouter.ts:294, socketTable.ts:248, socketPresence.ts:196). A bot timer firing after closeOwnership runs commitMove -> persistGameState (gamePersistence.ts:106-125 area, writeActiveGame has no ownsRoom check; ownsRoom is read only at tableRouter.ts:133) and, on a round end, handleRoundOver's stats/rating/replay writes.
correction: Reachable in production but narrow. Before closeOwnership the instance is still the legitimate lock holder, so bot moves there are harmless. The hazard window is closeOwnership to exit(0). In the healthy path drainPool (store/drainPool.ts:31-49) returns after 50 ms of quiet, so that window is usually well under the 1.2 s bot delay; it widens only when writes are in flight. The harm needs another instance to claim the freed lock and rehydrate in that window, then the old process to write a stale row (or double-write a round result if the round ends in the window). Cloud Run runs two revisions during every deploy (ADR-0003), and sockets dropped by io.close reconnect to the other revision within roughly 0.5-1.5 s, so it is possible but a few-ms-to-1-s race. The title's 'keep playing' is accurate; 'AFK' timers are slower (TURN_TIMEOUT) and are the less likely to land in the window.
priority_ok: P2: narrow race window, requires a rehydrate by another instance plus a timer inside the tail; not a routine data-loss path
fix_ok: Partly. Option A (clearRoomTimers for every activeGames key inside beginShutdown) is insufficient: it clears only afk/bot/autoStart (gameTimers.ts clearRoomTimers), not the per-user 'disconnect' timers, and an in-flight move handled after beginShutdown re-arms via armAfterMove. Option B (arm() refuses while shutting down) is the sound one, but isShuttingDown lives in gameRoom.ts and the flag has no reset (gameRoom.ts:148-162, tests/server/shutdownSeatLost.test.ts:1 notes it cannot be undone), so any test that arms timers after beginShutdown in the same process is poisoned; keep the guard on the timer-fire side (runBotTurn/afk callbacks return early) or inject it. Also the test should cover the closeOwnership-to-exit window, not just 'after beginShutdown'.

evidence: server/game/gamePersistence.ts:106-125 disposeGame: activeGames.delete, then `void releaseRoom(roomId)` immediately (:116), then the active_games delete queued on inRoomOrder (:117-124) behind any pending snapshot. correction: It is reachable on a single instance too, not just cross-instance: after activeGames.delete the router sees no game, and held still has the room until releaseRoom's microtask runs, so claimRoom (gameOwnership.ts:195) returns true and rehydrates from the not-yet-deleted row. Window is milliseconds (longer under DB stress), triggered by a rejoin or rematch vote arriving right after a dispose.

fix_ok: No. Releasing inside the same inRoomOrder chain after the delete keeps the room in `held` during the window, so the same-instance race stays open; worse, if a resurrection happens in that window, the deferred releaseRoom then runs `held.delete` / pg_advisory_unlock for a room whose resurrected game is live in activeGames, producing an unowned live table (unclaimedRooms() at gameOwnership.ts:246-248 is exactly that state). A sound fix is a tombstone (a `disposing` set consulted by rehydrateGame / claim) or deleting the row before removing the game from memory.

evidence: server/store/schemaDdl.ts:364-369 emits `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` for every column of every table on every boot, and ensureSchema (:489-496) runs them sequentially through the app pool with no lock_timeout or advisory lock (grep for advisory/lock_timeout finds none). Postgres takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the table before noticing the column exists.
correction: The count is larger than 'about 100': it is one statement per column across all tables (a few hundred). Because the app pool has a 5 s statement_timeout (db.ts:54), a boot that queues behind a long reader fails with a statement timeout and the server refuses to start (rethrown, :489 doc), while it also stalls queries queued behind it on that table. An advisory lock would only serialise concurrent boots, not remove this lock; skipping ALTERs for existing columns (information_schema or a single catalog read) is the change that removes the hazard.
fix_ok: Use the second option (skip existing columns); the pg_advisory_xact_lock option does not address the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE cost. Stays additive and idempotent per server/CLAUDE.md, and tests/server/schemaDdl.test.ts would need to cover the skip.

evidence: server/game/gamePersistence.ts:266 `candidates.map(r => r.id).filter((id) => !activeGames.has(id))` is the only liveness guard; the doc at :251-257 says 'A room still in the in-memory map is never a candidate, whatever its age', true only for this process. Candidates are chosen by rooms.createdAt < 24 h (:258-263) and then room_players, active_games and rooms rows are deleted (:268-279).
correction: Reachability is rare: it needs a room created more than 24 h ago that is still live on a different instance, i.e. a standing table running across a day (CONTEXT/GAME-RULES describe a table lasting until it breaks up), or a finished table held by connected players for a day. pruneAbandonedGames (:225-237) already uses updated_at and is cluster-safe.
fix_ok: Sound: excluding rows with a recent active_games.updated_at (written on every move) makes the guard cluster-wide; waiting lobbies have no active_games row and are covered by the age check.

evidence: server/socket/socketSafety.ts:265-280: the uncaughtException handler logs fatal, flushes the logger and calls process.exit(1) immediately; nothing waits for roomWriteTails (gamePersistence.ts inRoomOrder) or releases locks (the ownership connection dies with the process). conflict: socketSafety.ts:275-277: "Exiting is unconditional either way — a guard that could be skipped by a transport that never flushed would be no guard." and CLAUDE.md 'No self-defeating safeguards'. A drain-then-exit path that can hang on a bad process is the shape this rule warns about.
